Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly tokens & peak TPS

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can run a pricing model and come back with an apples-to-apples Hosted API proposal: 

- Expected monthly token volume (best estimate or range)
- Typical/expected peak TPS and whether you see multi-minute sustained peaks vs short bursts
- Target budget range or target $/1M tokens you have in mind (helps us size committed vs pay-as-you-go options)

I attached a short usage-estimate-template.xlsx to make the volumes easier to share if you have them. If easier, a quick reply with ballpark numbers is totally fine.

Next steps: once we have those numbers, Marissa will draft 2 pricing scenarios (commit tier + payg), and we can set a 30-min follow-up to walk through unit economics and any enterprise terms.

Thanks —
Ben

Ben —

Appreciate the follow-up and template. Quick answers below (ballpark):

- Expected monthly tokens: ~150,000,000 to 250,000,000 tokens/month (we scale quickly if initial model improves conversion)
- Peak TPS: we see spikes up to ~18 TPS for short bursts (30–60s) during batch jobs and up to 7 TPS steady during business hours. We do have occasional runs that spike higher for short windows but rare (>30 TPS would be unusual).
- Budget: early-stage budget target is roughly $800–1,000 per 1M tokens (we want to understand committed pricing vs payg). Our procurement team prefers predictable unit economics if we commit.

I attached our Q2 usage CSV to give you a feel for traffic patterns. Happy to jump on a follow-up next week — Thu mornings usually work.

Thanks,
Olivia Turner
Head of Platform | FinStack
olivia@finstack.com

Team —

Thanks Olivia for the numbers. Based on FinStack's 150–250M/month range and peak ~18 TPS, here are two quick scenarios to prepare for pricing ops:

1) Commit scenario (12-month):
   - Commit: 200M tokens/month
   - Unit price (1M): $700
   - Monthly commit cost: $140,000
   - Notes: includes 10% burst buffer, SLA 99.9, billed monthly; overage at $800/1M

2) Pay-as-you-go (no commit):
   - Unit price (1M): $1,000
   - Notes: no long-term commitment, ideal if uncertain on growth; may see higher latency during extreme spikes without reserved capacity

Questions/assumptions:
- Are the spikes truly short (30–60s)? If they can sustain >3 minutes frequently, we should recommend reserved capacity for consistent throughput.
- Do they need guaranteed TPS during batch jobs? We should confirm acceptable latency SLOs for peak periods.

I can draft a short MAP and pricing worksheet once Ben confirms whether Olivia is fine with a Thu AM follow-up. Also linking the HubSpot deal (RDW-2389) and a draft MAP that we can share.

-Marissa
